messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

Using summary(my.ergm)$coefs[,4] will extract the p-values as a vector, 
removing the header info in the process. If the rest of your code with 
all your models is writen as a loop, then you can simply have a line 
saving this vector into a different column of a data.frame (or any other 
similar object type). If you want to pull out the names of the terms as 
well to populate the row names of the data frame, then use 
rownames(summary(my.ergm)$coefs). When you're done you can export the 
full table into a variety of other formats using standard R functions 
(e.g. write.csv).

I hope that helps,
Steve

messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Actually, p-values are computed each time you ask for a summary of an 
ergm model [summary(my.model)]. Unfortunately, the "summary.ergm" 
function is not designed to store p-values, but a very slight 
modification of this function, like below, is possible:

###  Just copy the code below and then type 
mespval<-pvalergm(<my_ergm_model>) to store your p-values...

pvalergm<-function (object, ...)
{
     pseudolikelihood <- is.null(object$samplesize) || 
is.na(object$samplesize) # si $mcmcsamplesize n'est pas nul ou manquant, 
cela veut dire que l'estimation ne s'est pas faite par pseudolikelihood.
     independence <- is.dyad.independent(object) # mod?le ? ind?pendance 
dyadique?
     if (any(is.na(object$coef)) & !is.null(object$mplefit)) {
         object$coef[is.na(object$coef)] <- 
object$mplefit$coef[is.na(object$coef)]
     } # Si un des estimateurs ML obtenus par MCMC manque, remplace par 
les estimateurs Max pseudolikelihood. 

     if (is.null(object$hessian) && is.null(object$covar)) {
         return()
     }    # si la matrice hessienne ET la matrice des covariances 
estim?es (covar) n'existent pas, ne renvoie rien. La suite s'applique 
aux autres situations:
     nodes <- network.size(object$network)  # nb de nodes
     dyads <- network.dyadcount(object$network) # nb de dyades
     if (is.null(object$covar)) {
         asycov <- try(robust.inverse(-object$hessian), silent = TRUE)
         if (inherits(asycov, "try-error")) {
             asycov <- diag(1/diag(-object$hessian))
         } # si $covar est null, essaie de calculer asycov ? partir de 
$hessian
     } 

     else {
         asycov <- object$covar # si covar existe, asycov en est une copie.
	## Le if qui suit me para?t bizarre, car jamais TRUE? C'est p? une 
ancienne partie de code qui a ?t? d?sactiv?e...
         if (FALSE & !pseudolikelihood & !independence) {
             if (is.directed(object$network)) {
                 mdyads <- nodes * (nodes - 1)
             }
             else {
                 mdyads <- nodes * (nodes - 1)/2
             }
             asycov <- asycov * mdyads/dyads
             object$mc.se <- object$mc.se * sqrt(mdyads/dyads)
         }
     }
     rownames(asycov) <- names(object$coef)
     colnames(asycov) <- rownames(asycov)
     asyse <- diag(asycov) # asyse = variance des param?tres
     asyse[asyse < 0 | is.infinite(object$coef) | object$offset] <- NA
     asyse <- sqrt(asyse) # asyse = ecart-type des param?tres
     if (any(is.na(asyse) & !object$offset) & !is.null(object$mplefit)) {
         if (is.null(object$mplefit$covar)) {
             if (!is.null(object$mplefit$covar)) {
                 mpleasycov <- try(robust.inverse(-object$mplefit$hessian),
                   silent = TRUE)
                 if (inherits(mpleasycov, "try-error")) {
                   mpleasycov <- diag(1/diag(-object$mplefit$hessian))
                 }
                 asyse[is.na(asyse)] <- sqrt(diag(mpleasycov))[is.na(asyse)]
             }
         }
         else {
             mpleasycov <- object$mplefit$covar
             asyse[is.na(asyse)] <- sqrt(diag(mpleasycov))[is.na(asyse)]
         }
     } # Si certains ?carts-types de param?tres ne sont pas disponibles 
(valeur NA, voir ligne 39), remplace les par les ?carts-types trouv?s 
avec la MPLE.
     asyse <- matrix(asyse, ncol = length(asyse))
     colnames(asyse) <- colnames(asycov)

   dyads <- network.dyadcount(object$network)
   nodes <- network.size(object$network)
   if (!is.null(object$Z.mkl)) {
         p <- ncol(object$Z.mkl)
     }
     else {
         p <- 0
     }
   if (!is.null(object$cluster)) {
         df <- length(object$coef) + object$ngroups * (p + 2) -
             1

messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet help list,

I'm attempting to calculate a similarity measure among individuals' local networks in statnet.  The network is set up so that:

1) Each node in my network has values stored on five different vertex attributes (called trait1, trait2, trait3, trait4, and trait5.)
2) Each node is directly connected to up to 8 other nodes (but may be connected to fewer). 

For each node, I'd like to create an index measuring their level of similarity to their directly connected neighbors, where the index is calculated by:

number of similarities to neighbors / total possible similarities to neighbors

So, for example, if node A is connected to node B and only B, and A and B have identical values on trait1 and trait2, but not trait3, trait4, and trait5, then A's similarity index would be 2/5.  

If node C was directly connected to node D and node E, and C had the same values on trait1 and trait2 with D, but had no similar values with E, then C's similarity index should be 2/10. 

How would I be able to create this measure for all nodes in the network?  Any help or pointers would be appreciated!

Many thanks,
Jack

---
